questions.question:
Two masses of 1 kg and 2 kg were dropped from a height of 3.2 metres. Their respective velocities just before touching the ground will be:

(Assume acceleration due to gravity g = 10 m/s²)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**8 m/s for both**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The velocities of objects falling freely under gravity are independent of their masses.
 
• Both the 1 kg and 2 kg masses will experience the same acceleration due to gravity (g = 10 m/s²).
 
• The velocity just before touching the ground is determined by the equation v = sqrt{2gh}, where g is the acceleration due to gravity and h is the height from which the object is dropped.
 
• Using the formula v = sqrt{2 times 10 times 3.2} = sqrt{64} = 8 {m/s}, both masses will have the same velocity just before hitting the ground.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Acceleration due to Gravity:**

 
 
• Gravity is a fundamental force that attracts objects towards the center of the Earth.
 
• The value of acceleration due to gravity near Earth's surface is approximately 9.8 m/s² but is commonly approximated as 10 m/s² for simplicity in calculations.
 
• The value of gravity can vary depending on location, altitude, and Earth's irregular shape.
 
 
 
• **Free Fall:**
 
 
• When an object is dropped, and the only force acting on it is gravity, it is said to be in free fall.
 
• Objects in free fall accelerate at a constant rate due to gravity, regardless of their mass.
 
 
 
• **Formula for Velocity in Free Fall:**
 
 
• The velocity of an object just before hitting the ground can be found using the formula v = sqrt{2gh}, where g is the gravitational acceleration and h is the height.
 
• This equation assumes there is no air resistance.
 
 
 
• **Mass and Gravity:**
 
 
• In the absence of air resistance, all objects fall at the same rate regardless of their mass. This was famously demonstrated by Galileo.

questions.question: The igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks are interconvertible through a continuous process called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**rock cycle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The rock cycle is a continuous process through which rocks are transformed from one type to another over geological time scales.
 
• It involves the formation, breakdown, and reformation of rocks due to various geological processes.
 
• Igneous rocks can be broken down into sediments that form sedimentary rocks, which can then be subjected to heat and pressure to become metamorphic rocks.
 
• Metamorphic rocks can melt to form magma, which cools to become igneous rocks, thus completing the cycle.
 
• The rock cycle is driven by Earth's internal heat, plate tectonics, and surface processes like weathering and erosion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Igneous Rocks**

 
 
• Formed from the cooling and solidification of magma or lava.
 
• Examples include granite (intrusive) and basalt (extrusive).
 
 
 
• **Sedimentary Rocks**
 
 
• Formed from the accumulation and lithification of sediments.
 
• Examples include sandstone, limestone, and shale.
 
 
 
• **Metamorphic Rocks**
 
 
• Formed from the alteration of existing rocks due to high heat, pressure, or chemically active fluids.
 
• Examples include marble (from limestone) and schist (from shale).
 
 
 
• **Weathering and Erosion**
 
 
• Weathering is the breakdown of rocks at Earth's surface due to atmospheric conditions.
 
• Erosion involves the removal and transportation of weathered material by natural agents like water, wind, and ice.

questions.question: 'Sange Meel Se Mulaqat' is the documentary of which famous musician?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bismillah Khan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bismillah Khan** was a renowned Indian musician credited with popularizing the shehnai, a traditional Indian wind instrument.
 
• The documentary **'Sange Meel Se Mulaqat'** focuses on the life and musical journey of Bismillah Khan.
 
• Bismillah Khan received India's highest civilian honors, including the **Bharat Ratna** in 2001.
 
• He performed at the Red Fort on India's first Independence Day in 1947, marking the beginning of a tradition.
 
• Bismillah Khan's contribution to Indian classical music is celebrated globally, and he is remembered as a cultural icon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shehnai**

 
 
• The shehnai is a double-reed instrument traditional to India, often used in auspicious occasions and classical music.
 
• It is similar to the oboe and is known for its rich and soulful sound.
 
• Bismillah Khan is credited with elevating the shehnai from a folk instrument to one of classical status.
 
 
 
• **Bharat Ratna**
 
 
• It is the highest civilian award in India, instituted in 1954.
 
• The award recognizes exceptional service towards the advancement of art, literature, and science, and in recognition of public service of the highest order.
 
 
 
• **Indian Classical Music**
 
 
• It is divided into two major traditions: Hindustani (North Indian) and Carnatic (South Indian) music.
 
• Indian classical music is characterized by its raga (melodic framework) and tala (rhythmic patterns).
 
• Prominent instruments include the sitar, tabla, and shehnai.
 
 
 
• **Independence Day Performance**
 
 
• Bismillah Khan's performance at the Red Fort on August 15, 1947, is a historic moment in Indian history.
 
• His shehnai rendition signified the dawn of India's independence from British rule.

questions.question: Who among the following adopted the policy of consolidation in place of expansion by eliminating the rebels?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ghiyasuddin Balban**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ghiyasuddin Balban was the Sultan of Delhi from 1266 to 1287.
 
• He adopted a policy of consolidation by eliminating the rebels and maintaining strict control over his territories.
 
• Balban is known for his strong centralized administration and efforts to strengthen the Sultanate against internal and external threats.
 
• He implemented a policy of "blood and iron" to suppress revolts and rebellions, ensuring the stability and security of his rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shamsuddin Iltutmish**

 
 
• Iltutmish was the third Sultan of Delhi and a prominent ruler of the Mamluk dynasty.
 
• He is known for consolidating the Delhi Sultanate and introducing important administrative reforms.
 
• Iltutmish completed the construction of the Qutub Minar in Delhi.
 
• He introduced the silver tanka and the copper jital, standardizing the monetary system of the Sultanate.
 
 
 
• **Raziya**
 
 
• Raziya, also known as Razia Sultan, was the first and only female ruler of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• She ruled from 1236 to 1240 and was known for her administrative skills and efforts to promote gender equality.
 
• Raziya faced significant opposition from the nobility and was eventually overthrown.
 
 
 
• **Nasiruddin Mahmud**
 
 
• Nasiruddin Mahmud was the Sultan of Delhi from 1246 to 1266.
 
• He was a nominal ruler, with real power being held by his deputy, Ghiyasuddin Balban.
 
• Mahmud's reign is noted for the consolidation of the Sultanate's administration and military.
 
 
 
• **Ghiyasuddin Balban's Policies**
 
 
• Balban emphasized a strong and centralized administration to ensure the Sultanate's stability.
 
• He implemented a strict policy of law and order, using harsh measures to suppress rebellions and maintain control.
 
• Balban's reign marked the beginning of the consolidation of the Sultanate, setting the stage for future rulers.

questions.question: 'The Namesake', 'Unaccustomed Earth' and 'The Lowland' are novels written by who among the following authors?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jhumpa Lahiri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Jhumpa Lahiri** is a renowned American author known for her works exploring the Indian immigrant experience in the United States.
 
• Her debut short story collection, **"Interpreter of Maladies"**, won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction in 2000.
 
• **"The Namesake"** (2003) is a novel by Lahiri that was also adapted into a successful film directed by Mira Nair.
 
• **"Unaccustomed Earth"** (2008) is a collection of short stories that debuted at number one on The New York Times bestseller list.
 
• **"The Lowland"** (2013) was shortlisted for the Man Booker Prize and the National Book Award for Fiction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Interpreter of Maladies:**

 
 
• This is a collection of nine short stories by Jhumpa Lahiri, published in 1999.
 
• The collection deals with the lives of Indians and Indian Americans who are caught between their roots and the "New World."
 
• It won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction and the Hemingway Foundation/PEN Award in 2000.
 
 
 
• **The Namesake:**
 
 
• The novel explores themes of identity, cultural assimilation, and the generational gap within immigrant families.
 
• It tells the story of Gogol Ganguli, an American-born son of Indian immigrants, and his struggle with his identity.
 
 
 
• **Unaccustomed Earth:**
 
 
• A collection of eight stories that focus on the Bengali American community.
 
• The book explores themes of family, migration, and the diasporic experience.
 
• It received critical acclaim and was named one of the top ten books of the year by The New York Times Book Review.
 
 
 
• **The Lowland:**
 
 
• The novel is set in both India and the United States, and deals with themes of political unrest and personal loss.
 
• The story revolves around two brothers, one who gets involved in the Naxalite movement in India and the other who moves to the US for higher studies.
 
• It was shortlisted for the Man Booker Prize in 2013.

questions.question: Which of the following types of emergencies is declared under Article 360 of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Financial Emergency**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 360 of the Indian Constitution empowers the President of India to declare a Financial Emergency if they are satisfied that the financial stability or credit of India or any part of its territory is threatened.
 
• During a Financial Emergency, the executive authority of the Union extends to giving directions to any State to observe certain canons of financial propriety or such other directions as deemed necessary.
 
• Article 360 allows the President to reduce the salaries and allowances of all or any class of persons serving in the State and the Union.
 
• Under the Financial Emergency, the President can also reserve all money bills or other financial bills for their consideration after they are passed by the legislature of the State.
 
• No Financial Emergency has been declared in India so far.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Emergency (Article 352)**

 
 
• Declared on grounds of war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.
 
• It results in a modification of the federal structure of India, leading to a centralization of power.
 
• During National Emergency, fundamental rights under Article 19 are automatically suspended, and other rights can also be suspended by a presidential order.
 
 
 
• **State Emergency (Article 356)**
 
 
• Also known as President's Rule, it can be proclaimed on the failure of constitutional machinery in a state.
 
• During President's Rule, the state legislature is either dissolved or suspended, and the state comes under the direct control of the central government.
 
• The Governor administers the state in the name of the President.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Emergency**
 
 
• It is another term used for State Emergency under Article 356.
 
• It occurs when a state government is unable to function according to the constitutional provisions.
 
• This provision has been used numerous times since independence.
 
 
 
• **Parliamentary Approval**
 
 
• A Financial Emergency must be approved by both houses of Parliament within two months of its declaration.
 
• If approved, it remains in force indefinitely until it is revoked by the President.
 
• The resolution approving the Financial Emergency needs to be passed by a simple majority.

questions.question: When is the National Unity Day celebrated in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fri Oct 31 2025 00:00:00 GMT+0530 (India Standard Time)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• National Unity Day, also known as **Rashtriya Ekta Diwas**, is celebrated in India on **October 31** every year.
 
• This day commemorates the birth anniversary of **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**, who played a key role in the unification of India.
 
• It was introduced by the Government of India in **2014** to honor Sardar Patel's contributions to national integration.
 
• Various events such as the **"Run for Unity"** are organized across the country to mark this occasion.
 
• The day emphasizes the importance of maintaining the country's unity and integrity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**

 
 
• Also known as the **"Iron Man of India"**.
 
• First Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of independent India.
 
• Played a crucial role in the integration of over 500 princely states into the Indian Union.
 
• His efforts and strategies were pivotal in maintaining the nation's unity post-independence.
 
 
 
• **Statue of Unity**
 
 
• Located in the state of Gujarat, India.
 
• It is the world's tallest statue, standing at a height of 182 meters (597 feet).
 
• Dedicated to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and inaugurated on October 31, 2018.
 
• Symbolizes Patel's vision of a united India.
 
 
 
• **Run for Unity**
 
 
• An annual event organized on National Unity Day.
 
• Aims to promote national integration and communal harmony.
 
• Participants from various walks of life join to reinforce the message of unity.
 
 
 
• **National Unity Day Pledge**
 
 
• People take a pledge to preserve the unity, integrity, and security of the nation.
 
• Emphasizes the importance of working towards a stronger and more unified India.
 
• Often recited in schools, colleges, and government offices on this day.

questions.question: Which material was largely used to build the stupa at Piprahwa in uttar pradesh ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bricks**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The stupa at Piprahwa in Uttar Pradesh is one of the earliest Buddhist stupas in India.
 
• It was constructed using bricks, which was a common building material in ancient Indian architecture.
 
• The stupa is believed to date back to the time of Emperor Ashoka, around the 3rd century BCE.
 
• Excavations at the site have revealed a significant number of relics associated with the Buddha, suggesting the stupa's religious importance.
 
• The use of bricks in the construction provided durability and a method to easily create the dome-like structure typical of stupas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stupa Architecture:**

 
 
• A stupa is a mound-like or hemispherical structure containing relics and used as a place of meditation.
 
• The structure typically includes a dome (anda), a base (medhi), and a railing (vedika).
 
• Some stupas, like the Great Stupa at Sanchi, are decorated with intricate carvings and sculptures.
 
 
 
• **Emperor Ashoka:**
 
 
• Ashoka was an Indian emperor of the Maurya Dynasty who ruled almost all of the Indian subcontinent from c. 268 to 232 BCE.
 
• He is remembered for his role in spreading Buddhism across Asia and his efforts to propagate Buddhist values through edicts and monuments.
 
 
 
• **Archaeological Excavations:**
 
 
• Excavations at Piprahwa have unearthed a variety of significant artifacts, including reliquaries and ancient inscriptions.
 
• These findings have provided valuable insights into early Buddhist practices and the spread of Buddhism in India.
 
 
 
• **Brick Construction:**
 
 
• Bricks have been used in construction since ancient times, offering advantages such as uniformity, strength, and durability.
 
• In ancient India, bricks were typically made from local clay and baked in kilns to ensure longevity.

questions.question: How many components are there in the New India Literacy Program (NILP) scheme launched by the Union Ministry of Education in March 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Five**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The New India Literacy Program (NILP) scheme was launched by the Union Ministry of Education in March 2023.
 
• The NILP scheme aims to achieve universal literacy by focusing on both basic literacy and numeracy.
 
• There are **five components** in the NILP scheme.
 
• The program targets all non-literates aged 15 years and above in the country.
 
• The scheme is aligned with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, which emphasizes adult education and lifelong learning.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020**

 
 
• NEP 2020 is a comprehensive framework to guide the development of education in India.
 
 
• **Adult Education**
 
 
• Adult education refers to the practice of teaching and educating adults.
 
• It aims to improve literacy, numeracy, and essential life skills among adults.
 
• Adult education programs are crucial for achieving sustainable development goals.
 
• They help in enhancing employment opportunities and overall socio-economic development.
 
 
 
• **Basic Literacy and Numeracy**
 
 
• Basic literacy refers to the ability to read and write simple texts.
 
• Numeracy involves basic mathematical skills, such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.
 
• Both are essential for personal and professional development.
 
• Improving literacy and numeracy rates is a priority for many educational programs worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Lifelong Learning**
 
 
• Lifelong learning is the continuous pursuit of knowledge for personal or professional reasons.
 
• It enhances social inclusion, active citizenship, and personal development.
 
• Lifelong learning can be formal, non-formal, or informal.
 
• It is a key component of the NEP 2020 and the NILP scheme.

questions.question: In June 2023, which country conferred the 'Order of the Nile' award on Narendra Modi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Egypt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In June 2023, Egypt conferred the 'Order of the Nile' award on Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
 
• The 'Order of the Nile' is the highest state honor awarded by the government of Egypt.
 
• This award was given to Narendra Modi in recognition of his efforts to strengthen the bilateral relationship between India and Egypt.
 
• The award ceremony took place during Modi's visit to Egypt, where he engaged in various diplomatic and strategic discussions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Order of the Nile**

 
 
• The Order of the Nile is Egypt's highest state honor, established in 1915.
 
• It is awarded to both Egyptian and foreign nationals for outstanding services and contributions.
 
• The order consists of a collar, a star, and a sash worn with an insignia.
 
• Prominent recipients include heads of state, prime ministers, and other distinguished personalities.
 
 
 
• **India-Egypt Relations**
 
 
• India and Egypt share a rich history of strong bilateral ties, dating back to ancient civilizations.
 
• Both countries collaborate in various fields such as defense, trade, and cultural exchange.
 
• Recent engagements have focused on enhancing strategic partnerships and economic cooperation.
 
 
 
• **Diplomatic Awards**
 
 
• Diplomatic awards are honors given by a country to foreign nationals to recognize their contribution to bilateral relations.
 
• These awards can be in the form of medals, orders, or decorations.
 
• Such awards strengthen diplomatic ties and acknowledge mutual respect and cooperation.
 
 
 
• **State Visits**
 
 
• State visits are formal visits by a head of state to another country, typically involving high-level diplomatic meetings.
 
• These visits often result in the signing of agreements and the announcement of joint initiatives.
 
• State visits are significant for fostering international relations and cooperation.

questions.question: According to National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2023 (A Progress Review), what was the proportion of population in multidimensional poverty (Headcount Ratio) in urban India in 2019-2021?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.0527**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) measures multiple deprivations at the household level across health, education, and standard of living dimensions.
 
• The proportion of the population in multidimensional poverty in urban India for the period 2019-2021 was 0.0527, as per the National MPI 2023 report.
 
• The MPI uses data from the National Family Health Survey (NFHS) to compute the multidimensional poverty index.
 
• The MPI not only reflects the incidence of poverty but also its intensity, offering a more comprehensive understanding of poverty.
 
• The 2023 report shows progress in urban poverty reduction efforts, reflecting improvements in living standards, education, and health.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Family Health Survey (NFHS)**

 
 
• It is a large-scale, multi-round survey conducted in a representative sample of households throughout India.
 
• The survey provides essential data on health, nutrition, family welfare, and related issues.
 
• NFHS-5, conducted in 2019-2021, provided the data used for the National MPI 2023.
 
 
 
• **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)**
 
 
• Developed by the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
 
• It measures acute poverty by considering multiple deprivations across health, education, and living standards.
 
• The MPI identifies both the share of people who are multidimensionally poor and the average number of deprivations each poor person experiences.
 
 
 
• **Urban Poverty**
 
 
• Refers to poverty in urban areas, characterized by lack of access to adequate housing, sanitation, clean water, and other essential services.
 
• Urban poverty is often exacerbated by rapid urbanization, leading to the growth of slums and informal settlements.
 
• Policies aimed at reducing urban poverty focus on improving infrastructure, access to education, health services, and employment opportunities.
 
 
 
• **Policy Implications**
 
 
• The MPI provides a framework for policymakers to design targeted interventions to address multiple dimensions of poverty.
 
• It helps in monitoring the effectiveness of poverty reduction programs and policies over time.
 
• Data from the MPI can guide resource allocation to areas where poverty is most acute.

questions.question: In which of the followings years was the National Population Policy of India released?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Population Policy (NPP) of India was **released in the year 2000**.
 
• The policy aimed to address the unmet needs for contraception, healthcare infrastructure, and health personnel, and to provide integrated service delivery for basic reproductive and child health care.
 
• One of the key goals of the NPP 2000 was to achieve a **stable population by 2045**, consistent with the requirements of sustainable economic growth, social development, and environmental protection.
 
• The policy emphasized the need for **universal access to quality health care** and education, and it included strategies to promote delayed marriage and childbearing and to ensure child survival.
 
• It also set specific targets, such as reducing the Total Fertility Rate (TFR) to **replacement levels by 2010** and achieving universal immunization of children.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Health Policy 2017**

 
 
• The policy aims to achieve the highest possible level of health and well-being for all ages, through a preventive and promotive health care orientation in all developmental policies, and universal access to good quality health care services without anyone having to face financial hardship as a consequence.
 
• It also seeks to increase the life expectancy at birth from 67.5 to 70 by 2025.
 
• It emphasizes preventive healthcare, universal access to quality health services, and reducing out-of-pocket expenses for healthcare.
 
 
 
• **Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child and Adolescent Health (RMNCH+A) Strategy**
 
 
• This approach focuses on providing comprehensive care at all stages of life, starting from adolescence to childhood, reproductive age, pregnancy, and childbirth.
 
• It aims to reduce maternal and child mortality and improve the health and nutritional status of women and children.
 
 
 
• **Mission Indradhanush**
 
 
• Launched in December 2014, it aims to cover all those children who are either unvaccinated or are partially vaccinated against vaccine-preventable diseases.
 
• The mission focuses on improving immunization coverage and ensuring that children receive life-saving vaccines.
 
 
 
• **Total Fertility Rate (TFR)**
 
 
• It refers to the average number of children that would be born to a woman over her lifetime.
 
• Replacement level fertility is typically around 2.1 children per woman.
 
• Achieving a TFR of 2.1 is essential for population stabilization.

questions.question: A ______ happens in chess when a player gives up material during the initiation to seek some kind of compensation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gambit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A gambit in chess involves a player sacrificing material, usually a pawn, to gain a strategic advantage such as better positioning or initiative.
 
• The term "gambit" is derived from the Italian word "gambetto," meaning to trip someone.
 
• Common examples include the King’s Gambit and the Queen’s Gambit, which are well-known chess openings.
 
• Gambits can be accepted or declined by the opponent, leading to different lines of play.
 
• They are often used to surprise an opponent and force them into less familiar territory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **King’s Gambit**

 
 
• A historical chess opening starting with the moves 1.e4 e5 2.f4.
 
• It aims to control the center quickly and open lines for an aggressive attack.
 
• Popular during the 19th century, it is less common in modern high-level play due to its risky nature.
 
 
 
• **Queen’s Gambit**
 
 
• A classical chess opening starting with 1.d4 d5 2.c4.
 
• The objective is to offer the c4 pawn to gain a strong central presence.
 
• It is considered one of the most reliable and strategic openings in chess.
 
 
 
• **Accepted vs. Declined Gambits**
 
 
• In an accepted gambit, the opponent takes the offered material.
 
• In a declined gambit, the opponent avoids taking the material, instead focusing on other strategic goals.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Purpose**
 
 
• Gambits are used to disrupt the opponent’s plans and create dynamic positions.
 
• They often lead to complex and tactical middle games.

questions.question:
match the political parties of British India in column A with their respective founders in column B.

<div
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1: a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **All India Forward Bloc** was founded by **Subhash Chandra Bose** in 1939 after he resigned from the Indian National Congress.
 
• **Arya Samaj** was founded by **Dayananda Sarasvati** in 1875 to promote values and practices based on the infallibility of the Vedas.
 
• **The Congress Socialist Party** was founded by **Jai Prakash Narayan** in 1934 as a socialist caucus within the Indian National Congress.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subhash Chandra Bose**

• Bose formed the Indian National Army (INA) to fight against British rule.
 
 
 
• **Dayananda Sarasvati**

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about the Union Government budget in India?

a. The Budget reflects the vision of the government in fulfilling the aspirations of people.

b. The Budget is the summary report of the financial performance of the government in power.

c. The Budget provides details of expenditures meted out by various Union Government ministries.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All a, b and c**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Union Government budget in India is a comprehensive financial statement that outlines the government's economic vision and policy priorities.
 
• It reflects the vision of the government in fulfilling the aspirations of the people by detailing plans for development and reforms (statement a).
 
• The Budget also serves as a summary report of the financial performance of the government in power, providing insights into revenue and expenditure (statement b).
 
• Furthermore, the Budget provides detailed accounts of expenditures incurred by various Union Government ministries and departments (statement c).
 
• The Union Budget is presented annually by the Finance Minister in Parliament and includes both revenue and capital budget estimates for the upcoming fiscal year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Revenue Budget**

 
 
• Comprises the government's revenue receipts (tax and non-tax revenues) and the expenditure met from these revenues.
 
• Revenue expenditures are those that do not result in the creation of assets, such as salaries, subsidies, and interest payments.
 
 
 
• **Capital Budget**
 
 
• Includes capital receipts (borrowings and disinvestments) and capital expenditures (outlays on asset creation like infrastructure).
 
• Capital expenditures are aimed at enhancing the productive capacity of the economy.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal Deficit**
 
 
• It is the gap between total revenue and total expenditure of the government, excluding borrowings.
 
• A high fiscal deficit indicates the government is borrowing more to meet its expenses.
 
 
 
• **Union Budget Presentation**
 
 
• The Union Budget is presented by the Finance Minister in the Parliament, typically on February 1st each year.
 
• The budget covers the financial year, which runs from April 1 to March 31 of the following year.

questions.question: Kaal Baisakhi belongs to which state from the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**West Bengal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kaal Baisakhi, also known as Nor'westers, is a local thunderstorm that occurs in the Indian state of **West Bengal**.
 
• These thunderstorms typically occur during the pre-monsoon season, from March to May.
 
• The storms are characterized by sudden, powerful winds, heavy rain, and occasionally hail.
 
• Kaal Baisakhi plays a crucial role in providing relief from the intense heat of the summer and in aiding the growth of crops like jute and paddy in West Bengal.
 
• This weather phenomenon is a significant aspect of the climate in the region and greatly influences the agricultural patterns.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Terminology:**

 
 
• The term "Kaal Baisakhi" is derived from the Bengali words "Kaal" meaning "fateful" and "Baisakhi" indicating the Bengali month of Baisakh (April-May).
 
 
 
• **Formation:**
 
 
• Kaal Baisakhi is formed due to the heating of the land, which causes the air to rise and form cumulonimbus clouds, leading to thunderstorms.
 
 
 
• **Impact:**
 
 
• While these storms are beneficial for agriculture, they can also cause significant damage to property, infrastructure, and can lead to fatalities.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Spread:**
 
 
• Besides West Bengal, Kaal Baisakhi also affects regions in Assam, Odisha, Bihar, and parts of Bangladesh.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• Historical records and local folklore often mention Kaal Baisakhi, emphasizing its long-standing presence and impact in the region.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true about Plastids?

options.text: Starch, oils and protein granules are stored in chromoplasts.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Starch, oils and protein granules are stored in chromoplasts.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Chromoplasts are primarily involved in the synthesis and storage of pigments, particularly carotenoids, which give red, yellow, and orange colors to plant tissues.
 
• Plastids, including chromoplasts, have their own DNA and ribosomes, indicating their evolutionary origin from endosymbiotic bacteria.
 
• Chloroplasts, another type of plastid, contain stroma, which is a fluid matrix that houses the enzymes necessary for the synthesis of organic molecules during photosynthesis.
 
• Amyloplasts are the type of plastids that store starch, while elaioplasts store oils and proteinoplasts store proteins, not chromoplasts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chloroplasts:**

 
 
• These are the most well-known plastids and are responsible for photosynthesis in plant cells.
 
• They contain chlorophyll, the green pigment that captures light energy.
 
• The inner membrane of chloroplasts surrounds the stroma and thylakoid membranes where the light-dependent reactions occur.
 
 
 
• **Leucoplasts:**
 
 
• These are non-pigmented plastids found in non-photosynthetic tissues of plants, such as roots and seeds.
 
• They are involved in the synthesis and storage of starches, oils, and proteins.
 
 
 
• **Endosymbiotic Theory:**
 
 
• This theory suggests that plastids like chloroplasts and mitochondria originated from free-living bacteria that were engulfed by ancestral eukaryotic cells.
 
• The evidence supporting this theory includes the presence of their own DNA and ribosomes within these organelles.
 
 
 
• **Function of Stroma:**
 
 
• The stroma is the site of the Calvin cycle, where carbon dioxide is fixed into glucose using ATP and NADPH generated in the light-dependent reactions.
 
• It contains enzymes, ribosomes, and small circular DNA molecules.

questions.question: In the animal kingdom, which of the following phyla includes animals with a segmented body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Annelida**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Annelida is a phylum of segmented worms, which includes earthworms, leeches, and marine worms.
 
• Members of the Annelida phylum have bodies divided into repetitive segments called metameres.
 
• This segmentation allows for greater flexibility and mobility, facilitating burrowing and other locomotive behaviors.
 
• Annelids possess a true coelom, a body cavity completely lined with mesoderm, which aids in the function of their hydrostatic skeleton.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Metamerism:** This refers to the segmentation of the body into a series of repeated units, which is a key characteristic of Annelida.
 
• **Closed Circulatory System:** Annelids have a closed circulatory system, meaning that blood is enclosed within blood vessels and is pumped by a heart.
 
• **Setae:** Many annelids possess small bristle-like structures called setae on each segment, which help in locomotion and anchorage.
 
• **Ecological Role:** Annelids play a significant role in soil health as decomposers and by aerating the soil, which is vital for plant growth.
 
• **Clitellum:** In earthworms, a thickened, glandular section of the body known as the clitellum secretes mucus during reproduction, aiding in the transfer of sperm and the formation of a cocoon for the developing embryos.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT associated with the Iron Age in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mehrauli iron pillar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Mehrauli iron pillar is a historical monument located in Delhi, India.
 
• This pillar is famous for its rust-resistant composition of metals and dates back to the Gupta period (around the 4th century AD).
 
• It is not associated with the Iron Age in India, which primarily spans from around 1500 BC to 200 BC.
 
• The pillar is believed to have been constructed during the reign of Chandragupta II (375-415 AD).
 
• The pillar's inscription and construction techniques are distinct from those of the Iron Age, which makes it an exceptional artifact from the Gupta period rather than the Iron Age.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iron Age in India**

 
 
• The Iron Age in India began around 1500 BC and lasted until approximately 200 BC.
 
• This period is characterized by the widespread use of iron tools and weapons, which significantly enhanced agricultural productivity and warfare.
 
• Notable cultures from this period include the Painted Grey Ware culture and the Northern Black Polished Ware culture.
 
• Iron smelting and metallurgy were significant advancements during this time, leading to the development of more durable and efficient tools.
 
 
 
• **Painted Grey Ware (PGW)**
 
 
• PGW is a type of pottery associated with the Vedic period in northern India.
 
• It dates back to the Iron Age and is characterized by its grey color and painted geometric designs.
 
• PGW sites are often linked to the early Indo-Aryan settlements in the region.
 
 
 
• **Northern Black Polished Ware (NBPW)**
 
 
• NBPW is a type of fine pottery that emerged during the later part of the Iron Age in India, around 700-200 BC.
 
• This pottery is known for its highly polished black surface and was used by the Mauryan Empire and other contemporary cultures.
 
• NBPW is considered a hallmark of urbanization and socio-economic development in ancient India.
 
 
 
• **Gupta Period**
 
 
• The Gupta period, spanning from the 4th to the 6th century AD, is known as the Golden Age of India.
 
• This era witnessed significant advancements in science, mathematics, astronomy, religion, and art.
 
• The Mehrauli iron pillar is an example of the high level of metallurgical skill achieved during this time.

questions.question: From which of the following countries has the Indian Constitution borrowed the concept of the Concurrent List?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Australia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The concept of the Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution has been borrowed from the Constitution of Australia.
 
• The Concurrent List allows both the Union and the State Governments to legislate on certain matters.
 
• This list includes subjects like marriage, bankruptcy, trade unions, and education.
 
• In case of a conflict between Union and State laws on a concurrent subject, the law made by the Union Government prevails.
 
• The inclusion of the Concurrent List ensures a balance of power and responsibilities between the central and state governments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union List**

 
 
• The Union List consists of subjects on which only the central government can legislate.
 
• It includes matters of national importance like defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, and railways.
 
• There are 97 subjects listed under the Union List in the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
 
 
• **State List**
 
 
• The State List comprises subjects on which only the state governments can legislate.
 
• It includes matters of local or state importance such as police, public health, and agriculture.
 
• There are 66 subjects listed under the State List in the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Seventh Schedule**
 
 
• The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution outlines the division of powers between the Union and State governments.
 
• It contains three lists: the Union List, the State List, and the Concurrent List.
 
• This schedule is crucial for maintaining the federal structure of India.
 
 
 
• **Residual Powers**
 
 
• Residual powers refer to subjects not mentioned in any of the three lists.
 
• According to the Indian Constitution, residual powers rest with the Union Government.
 
• This provision ensures that any new subject of legislation that arises is dealt with at the national level.

questions.question: __________ was launched by the Government of India in 2020 to make the country and its citizens independent and self-sufficient in all respects.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan was launched by the Government of India in **May 2020** to make the country and its citizens self-reliant.
 
• This initiative aims to provide a stimulus package of **INR 20 lakh crore**, which is equivalent to 10% of India's GDP.
 
• The Abhiyan focuses on five main pillars: Economy, Infrastructure, System, Vibrant Demography, and Demand.
 
• The goal is to promote local manufacturing, boost local markets, and reduce dependence on imports.
 
• The package covers various sectors, including MSMEs, agriculture, and public health, among others.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **MSME Sector**

 
 
• Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) are the backbone of the Indian economy, contributing significantly to GDP and employment.
 
• Under Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan, the government announced collateral-free automatic loans worth INR 3 lakh crore for MSMEs.
 
• The initiative also includes a Fund of Funds with a corpus of INR 10,000 crore to provide equity funding for MSMEs.
 
• Revised definition of MSMEs to include larger enterprises and allow them to take advantage of the schemes.
 
 
 
• **Agriculture Sector**
 
 
• The package includes INR 1 lakh crore for the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund for farm-gate infrastructure for farmers.
 
• The government also announced INR 20,000 crore for the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) to develop marine and inland fisheries.
 
• Reforms to amend the Essential Commodities Act and promote barrier-free inter-state trade of agricultural products.
 
• Focus on improving storage and logistics to reduce post-harvest losses.
 
 
 
• **Public Health**
 
 
• The package allocates INR 15,000 crore to strengthen public health infrastructure in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• Emphasis on ramping up testing facilities, creating additional hospital beds, and ensuring the availability of essential medical supplies.
 
• Enhanced focus on research and development of vaccines and treatments for COVID-19.
 
• Support for states to improve their healthcare systems and prepare for future health crises.

questions.question: Which of the following war dances is performed in Ngada festival and is performed by the tribes of Nagaland?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rengma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Rengma tribe is one of the indigenous tribes of Nagaland, India.
 
• The war dance performed by the Rengma tribe during the Ngada festival is a traditional dance that symbolizes bravery and valor.
 
• Ngada is a post-harvest festival celebrated by the Rengma Nagas, usually in late November.
 
• The dance is performed with traditional attire and weapons, showcasing the tribe's rich cultural heritage.
 
• Ngada festival is a significant cultural event for the Rengma tribe, involving various rituals, feasts, and dances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nagaland Tribes**

 
 
• Nagaland is home to 16 major tribes, each with its unique traditions and cultural practices.
 
• Some of the prominent tribes include Angami, Ao, Sumi, Lotha, and Chakhesang.
 
• Each tribe celebrates its own festivals, which are crucial to their cultural identity.
 
 
 
• **Ngada Festival**
 
 
• The Ngada festival marks the end of the agricultural year for the Rengma tribe.
 
• It involves rituals such as offerings to ancestors, community feasts, and traditional dances.
 
• The festival also serves as a time for reconciliation and strengthening community bonds.
 
 
 
• **War Dances in India**
 
 
• War dances are a significant part of many tribal cultures in India, symbolizing strength and unity.
 
• Other notable war dances include the Bihu dance of Assam and the Kalaripayattu of Kerala.
 
• These dances often incorporate traditional weapons and elaborate costumes.
 
 
 
• **Traditional Attire and Weapons**
 
 
• During the war dance, participants wear traditional attire that often includes feathers, beads, and animal skins.
 
• Weapons such as spears, shields, and swords are used as part of the dance to demonstrate warrior skills.
 
• These elements are integral to preserving the historical and cultural narratives of the tribes.

questions.question: Which edition of the Pro Kabaddi League was started in December 2023?

__
 
• The 10th edition of the Pro Kabaddi League commenced in December 2023.
 
• The Pro Kabaddi League (PKL) was first launched in 2014, and it has gained immense popularity over the years.
 
• PKL is a professional-level kabaddi league in India, organized by Mashal Sports and backed by Star India.
 
• Each season of the league features teams representing various cities across India, competing in a franchise-based format.
 
• The league has played a significant role in popularizing the sport of kabaddi in India and worldwide.

• The league was inspired by the success of the Kabaddi tournament at the 2006 Asian Games and the Kabaddi World Cup held in 2004.
 
• It was launched with the objective of transforming kabaddi into a professional sport with a large fan base.
 
• The inaugural season took place in 2014 with eight teams participating.
 
 
 
• **Format of PKL**
 
 
• The league follows a franchise-based model similar to that of the Indian Premier League (IPL) in cricket.
 
• Each team comprises players from various countries, including India, Iran, South Korea, and others.
 
• The league is played in a double round-robin format followed by playoffs and a final to determine the champion.

• PKL has significantly increased the popularity and viewership of kabaddi in India and internationally.
 
• The league has provided a platform for local talent to showcase their skills and gain recognition.
 
• It has also contributed to the economic growth of the sport by attracting sponsors, advertisers, and media coverage.

• The league has introduced technological advancements such as video referrals and data analytics to enhance the viewing experience.
 
• PKL has expanded its reach by broadcasting matches in multiple languages and on digital platforms.
 
• The league continues to innovate with new team formations, player auctions, and fan engagement activities.
